action_items.text: Review the minutes that were emailed and placed in the shared folder.
Make a decision on the remote control functions.
Design several different prototypes of user interfaces for the remote control and gather feedback on them.
Design a chip that works well with the user interface and isn't too complicated.
Find a long-lasting energy source that doesn't require frequent battery changes.
Ensure the infra-red signal is reliable and clear so users aren't frustrated by waving the remote.
Complete a questionnaire and a summary.
Put up the minutes and project documentation, including PowerPoint slides.
Complete individual work: Industrial Design (components concept), User Interface (user interface concept), and market trend watching.
Note any frustrations or issues that come up in the summary.

decisions.text: The group will proceed with the presentations in the order they were originally listed.
The team will not include teletext functionality in the new remote control design because it has been taken over by the internet.
The project will focus on television (T_V) rather than video or other media to keep it simple and quick.
The new design must use the corporate image: yellow color, black, and the slogan 'fashion in electronics' (emphasizing R_s).
The target group is defined as people aged 15 to 35 who have disposable income for technology.
Voice recognition will not be included as a function because it adds too much to the price and is not necessary for a remote.
The remote will be sold separately for 25 Euro.
The design will emphasize simplicity and fashion (usability).
The remote must include a feature to keep it from getting lost (e.g., a button to make it ring/beep).
The remote must have large, accessible buttons for essential functions.
Extra functions should be hidden away or not as prominent as main features.
The remote should be fashionable so it is not an eyesore on the coffee table.
The remote should have a long-life battery or a rechargeable option (e.g., charging station/cradle).
The remote should be designed to fit in living-room spaces (e.g., not too large to put on top of the TV).
